statement: You are given a string s of lowercase letters. You may add characters only to the front of s.
Return the shortest palindrome that can be made this way.

The characters to add are the reverse of whatever follows the longest palindromic prefix of s. That prefix can be found with the KMP LPS array of s + "#" + reverse(s): its last entry is the prefix's length.

examples.explanation: The longest palindrome at the start of s is "aacecaa" (7 characters). Only the final "a" lies outside it, so one "a" is added to the front.
Only the single character "a" is a palindromic prefix, so the reverse of "bcd", which is "dcb", is added to the front.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
